response_json.request: Add 0.2 mm chamfer to the hole edges to improve fitting.

actions.relational_constraint: The chamfer is applied to the edges of the hole.
actions.unresolved_reference: Identify the referenced hole or holes and their applicable edges in the original CAD model.
steps: Interpret the referenced hole as the complete coaxial transverse pin passage formed by the pin bores in clevis ear A and clevis ear B. This localization best matches the stated fitting intention because these bores directly receive and guide the mating clevis pin.

Locate clevis ear A in section SEC-03. Identify its cylindrical pin-bore face 0024, corresponding to Brep_id FACE 44, and the two circular boundary edges where that bore intersects outer side face 0021, Brep_id FACE 78, and inner side face 0023, Brep_id FACE 90.

Locate clevis ear B in section SEC-04. Identify its cylindrical pin-bore face 0028, corresponding to Brep_id FACE 46, and the two circular boundary edges where that bore intersects inner side face 0025, Brep_id FACE 89, and outer side face 0027, Brep_id FACE 79.

Confirm that the two cylindrical bore faces are coaxial, as required by the SEC-03 to SEC-04 coaxial relationship, and that all four selected circular edges belong to the same functional transverse pin passage.

Do not select the four vertical mounting bores in SEC-01. Those holes serve mounting fasteners, whereas the clevis pin bores are the geometry most directly associated with pin insertion, alignment, and improved fitting.
Create a direct edge-chamfer feature; no sketch plane, profile sketch, or extrusion is required for this operation.
Select the four circular bore-rim edges: the outer and inner rims of ear A and the inner and outer rims of ear B. Exclude the rounded crown edges, ear-root edges, and shell-transition edges.

Set the chamfer definition to an equal-distance chamfer with a size of 0.2 mm. Where the CAD system requires a second definition, use a 45-degree angle so the axial and radial setbacks are both 0.2 mm.
Apply the chamfer simultaneously to all four selected edges so the entrance, inter-ear transition rims, and exit of the coaxial pin passage receive consistent lead-ins.
Regenerate the solid and verify that the chamfer does not break through the ear side faces, intersect the rounded crowns, or remove significant bearing length from bore faces 0024 and 0028.

Inspect the result from the left, right, and top-right isometric views. Confirm that each ear has a uniform annular 0.2 mm chamfer at both ends of its bore and that the central cylindrical portions remain coaxial and at the original radius of 0.75.
Perform a final geometry check to ensure the model remains a single valid solid and that the new chamfers provide continuous, burr-free lead-in edges for insertion of the mating transverse pin.
